quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What should a driver do when entering public traffic from a driveway or private road?

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Wait for a safe gap and merge slowly into traffic.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol.
Amphetamines.
Anger.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving safety. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours has the same effect as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: This sign shape and color is a ____ sign.

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are used only to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: What colors do warning signs use to show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs showing upcoming hazards are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: Taking drugs along with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol alone.
Reduces the effect of alcohol on your driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter) can impair your brain function and driving ability. Combining alcohol with drugs increases your crash risk.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must travel at the exact speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign showing the maximum legal speed you may drive on this road. In bad weather or poor conditions, you must drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is separated by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: To safely cross a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, then proceed if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly drive under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, then proceed if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from either direction before crossing the tracks. Wait for all warning signals to clear before proceeding.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of fatal crashes. At speeds above 80 mph, survival chances are very low. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because it may cause other drivers to make risky passing moves.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Give yourself extra space to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is dangerous, especially right after rain starts. Your vehicle rides on a layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when there is heavy rain, standing water, or slush to prevent your wheels from losing grip.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, let others go first, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down so the driver behind you has enough space to pass. This lets them finish passing faster and more safely.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to look.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head and look through the rear window when backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Do not only rely on mirrors.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs mark?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you to yield to trains at a railroad crossing. Do not try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or pass pedestrians, cyclists, and scooter riders when the other lane is clear and it is safe.

questions.question: After a school bus stops and unloads children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not go until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Watch for children walking along the roadside after a school bus stops. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass carefully.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
Use your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait for traffic ahead to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way you do on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other cars.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your car needs more time to stop on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
A special speed zone.
An area where stereos must be quiet.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in back, and in front. Cars in these areas cannot be seen by the driver. These areas are called the "No zone."
